SNACS review rules and exceptions

Each target has a scene role and a lexical function. The function is typically an ancestor of the role, but can differ; preserve both labels when the example shows a construal.

Possessives/genitives: distinguish the relation expressed by the possessor form. An organization framed in relation to its members can be Org;Gestalt (e.g. strategies attributed to Stuart's organization). Ordinary possessors remain Possessor;Possessor (e.g. your money). An organization noun used as possessor may be OrgMember;Possessor (e.g. our business). Genitives of an attribute or quality can be Gestalt;Gestalt (e.g. ethical strategies).

Of phrases: amount/number + of + item can be QuantityItem;Whole (e.g. each of you). Of after an adjective of emotion/evaluation can be Stimulus;Topic (e.g. proud of contributions). Of indicating the force behind an event can be Force;Force (e.g. reap the rewards of a program).

Temporal expressions: since introducing a time point can be Time;Time. Throughout a time span can be Duration;Duration.

To phrases: a verb's addressee/recipient can be Recipient;Goal (e.g. recommend to anyone). Do not assume matching role and function: check whether the lexical construction construes the relation differently.

These are example-backed patterns, not unconditional rules; use sentence context and the guideline definitions for ambiguous cases.
